objective: Test the physically legal replacement for the invalid nine-bit-slice pseudo-dual-port idea: two complete nine-macro 1RW parent banks selected by a compile-time XOR of the six-bit row address. This is a stratified exact schedule fast-kill only; a positive result may nominate one mapping for a full same-ledger replay but cannot establish Conv or system speedup.

population.grain: 440 deterministic phases x all 3000 rows, stratified over all 10 samples and all four bottleneck Conv3x3 operators

dse.selection: minimum exact local issue-window cycles, tie-broken by smallest xor_mask

capacity.port_model: one access per bank per cycle; read and write may overlap only across different complete banks

gates.positive_action: Nominate only the best XOR mapping for one full-population same-ledger replay and matched macro accounting.
gates.negative_action: KILL the two-bank idea without RTL if either performance gate or the 240 KiB capacity gate fails.

fail_closed: The nine original macros are bit slices of one logical 1152-bit row and are never treated as independent row banks.
Both candidate banks contain all nine 128-bit slices; no same-bank read and write may occur in one cycle.
Arithmetic issues, parent edges, response ordering, forwarding, liveness dead-write elision and synchronous read latency remain identical to M505.
A stratified local speedup is not a full-pipeline, Conv, network or system speedup.
